propositions: At search exhaustion, completion verifier incorrectly banks `met=false` for absence-of-evidence, producing false FAIL verdicts when sufficient evidence exists but was not reached within the search budget

Banked completion criteria require a tri-state outcome (met, refuted, insufficient) to distinguish positive refutation from evidence exhaustion, carried as an optional `evidence_sufficient:false` marker alongside `met=false`

The bounded fallback banking path must invoke `CriterionBank.record_insufficient()` instead of the model-facing record tool to ensure the marker is framework-owned, the tool remains bool-only, and model `met=false` retains positive refutation semantics
Fallback-banked insufficient entries must preserve their marker through subsequent harvests from model output (preserve-on-overwrite), while genuine refutation (bare `met=false`) replaces it

All completion verdict consumers (schema validation, recovery finalizer, reconciliation, close gate, renderers, sidecar) must respect the marker and emit insufficient-evidence messaging instead of unmet-criteria guidance, while still maintaining fail-closed verdicts
